cut.reason: Background sources (e.g. a 2022 tissue-loss/metabolic-adaptation study in Int J Obes, and the classic Ballor & Poehlman exercise/diet-restriction meta-analysis) clearly describe RMR decline with caloric restriction, but full abstract text with a verbatim, quotable numeric RMR effect was not retrieved within the research budget for this session. This is flagged as the single most promising addition for a future pass, since it bears directly on the resting-metabolic-rate marker and the caloric_deficit_magnitude behavior already in this file.

cut.label: alcohol -> fat_mass and alcohol -> lean_mass (general, beyond visceral fat)
cut.reason: Alcohol's relationship with total fat mass and lean mass is confounded by total caloric intake and cannot be isolated with a randomized design (heavy, sustained drinking cannot be ethically randomized long-term); only the visceral-fat-specific, total-fat-mass-adjusted cohort finding (Chesters et al. 2026) was kept, because its adjustment for total fat mass isolates a body-fat-distribution effect rather than a generic caloric one.

cut.label: D-aspartic acid, Tribulus terrestris
cut.reason: These appear in the design document's Goal A (male vitality / testosterone) candidate list, not in this goal's (body composition and strength) candidate behaviors; out of scope for this file and not evaluated.

cut.label: resistance_training / creatine_monohydrate -> lean_mass and max_strength in general (young, non-aged) populations, as separate edges alongside the aged-specific ones
cut.reason: The literature for general/young populations is broadly consistent with (and larger in magnitude than) the aged-specific effects already included, but a second, non-overlapping verbatim-quotable meta-analysis was not pulled for this pass given the research budget; the aged-specific creatine finding and the mixed-age Lopez 2021 resistance-training finding were judged sufficient to establish both behaviors without duplicating the same claim twice.

cut.label: bilingualism_cognitive_reserve -> global_cognition_older (delay in dementia/symptom onset)
cut.reason: Evidence is observational/retrospective and framed as a delay in age-of-onset (Cohen's d = 0.32 for age-of-onset studies) rather than a score on a named instrument; prospective incidence-rate studies (the design least confounded by education/immigration/SES) show a much weaker, largely null effect (d = 0.10). Age-of-onset-delay framing structurally mirrors the 'years of life' mortality-style metric this design explicitly excludes, and no RCT is possible for a lifelong exposure like bilingualism, so the claim cannot be cleanly separated from cohort confounding (bilingual populations in these studies differ systematically in education and immigration history).

cut.label: omega3_supplementation -> global_cognition_older or processing_speed, using the 2025 dose-response meta-analysis (PMC12368174) showing broad positive effects
cut.reason: This more recent 58-RCT dose-response meta-analysis reports positive effects across multiple domains (perceptual speed, language, memory, visuospatial function, global cognition), which would directly contradict the shipped null edge (Cochrane 2012, MMSE, cognitively healthy older adults). Rather than shipping both and leaving the contradiction unresolved, the population-matched, instrument-named, healthy-older-adult-specific Cochrane null was kept because it isolates the exact population and instrument (MMSE) that the design's marker specifies; the broader dose-response review pools healthy and impaired populations and multiple cognitive tests without isolating a single clean healthy-adult claim in its abstract.

cut.label: acute_aerobic_exercise -> processing_speed or global cognition, using the individual-participant-data meta-analysis (Ishihara et al. 2021, PMID 34147558)
cut.reason: This IPD meta-analysis's abstract reports only a qualitative moderation pattern (pre-test performance moderates the after-effect of acute exercise) with no quantified effect size, so no number could be placed in the `effect` field without violating the requirement that every number in `effect` be derivable from the edge's own verbatim. Superseded here by Chang et al. 2012 and Ludyga et al. 2016, both of which report quantified Hedges' g values in their abstracts.

cut.label: caffeine -> working_memory or sustained_attention_rt in well-rested, non-sleep-deprived healthy adults (i.e., caffeine's 'baseline' effect outside of sleep loss)
cut.reason: The literature on caffeine in rested, habitual consumers is heavily confounded by reversal of overnight withdrawal (habitual drinkers test worse than their true baseline without their usual dose, so a 'benefit' partly reflects relief of withdrawal rather than net enhancement). No abstract-quantified meta-analysis isolating a clean non-deprived, non-habituated caffeine effect with a named instrument was retrieved within the research budget; only the sleep-restricted/deprived population edge (Frontiers 2026 military meta-analysis) is shipped, with this exact caveat given in its conditional_on field.

cut.label: creatine_monohydrate -> working_memory, using secondary/news coverage claiming 'creatine users performed better on working memory' (nutraingredients.com, bubsnaturals.com)
cut.reason: These are secondary/marketing summaries of the sleep-deprivation RCT (Gordji-Nejad et al.), but the PubMed abstract of that RCT itself names only 'logical and numerical tasks, language-related processing speed, and the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT)' as outcomes -- it does not use the phrase 'working memory' or report a working-memory-specific statistic. Shipping a working-memory edge from this source would require citing a paraphrase rather than the source's own verbatim, which the acceptance bar disallows.

cut.label: Alcohol -> anxiety_symptoms
cut.reason: No meta-analysis was found within the research budget that reports a clean, quantified pooled effect size for alcohol/AUD on a named anxiety instrument (GAD-7/STAI/HAM-A) with a verbatim-derivable number; available hits were either off-topic (PTSD neuroimaging papers matched by keyword overlap) or lacked a quantified anxiety-specific estimate.

cut.label: D-aspartic acid / Tribulus terrestris (expected null)
cut.reason: Not part of this goal's candidate list (these were Goal A/testosterone candidates); no mood-specific trials of either were identified as worth pursuing under the mood/anxiety goal, so they were not investigated here.

cut.label: St John's wort -> anxiety_symptoms
cut.reason: The literature on Hypericum focuses almost exclusively on depression outcomes; no dedicated meta-analysis isolating an anxiety-symptom instrument for St John's wort (as opposed to depression trials that happen to report an anxiety subscale) was found.

cut.label: Aerobic/resistance exercise -> cortisol (diurnal slope)
cut.reason: Pascoe 2017 (DOI 10.1016/j.psyneuen.2017.08.008) reports yoga/MBSR practices were associated with 'reduced evening cortisol, waking cortisol' but gives no quantified effect size or CI in the abstract, so no verbatim-derivable number could be extracted; the cortisol marker is instead covered via the mindfulness-based-interventions behavior using Rogerson et al 2024, which does report a quantified estimate.

cut.label: Loneliness-reduction intervention (e.g. befriending, social prescribing) -> depressive_symptoms as an RCT effect
cut.reason: Search effort found only observational/longitudinal-cohort evidence for the loneliness-depression relationship (Mann et al 2022, used above); no RCT meta-analysis of a loneliness-reduction intervention with a quantified depressive-symptom effect size was located within the research budget, so the behavior is represented only via the risk-factor direction, not an interventional reversal.

cut.label: Time in nature -> cortisol
cut.reason: Candidate searches for nature exposure and cortisol/HPA-axis outcomes returned disaster-exposure and natural-hazard mental health reviews (keyword collision on 'nature') rather than green-space/forest-bathing cortisol trials with a quantified pooled estimate; not pursued further given time budget.

cut.label: smoking_and_cessation -> cardiovascular_mortality and smoking_and_cessation -> cancer_incidence_mortality, cause-specific quantified
cut.reason: Jha 2013 (used for the all-cause mortality edges) reports only an all-cause hazard ratio in its abstract, not cause-specific breakdowns; other candidate papers found (Wang 2021 on cessation/weight-gain/CVD, Chang 2021 on smoking reduction) report CVD- or cancer-specific relative risks for narrower sub-questions (post-cessation weight gain, partial reduction rather than full cessation) that do not cleanly map to a general smoking-vs-never-smoking comparison for these two markers within the research budget.

cut.label: cardiorespiratory_fitness -> cardiovascular_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: The main available meta-analysis (Kodama 2009) pools CHD/CVD 'events' rather than cardiovascular deaths specifically, mixing fatal and non-fatal outcomes; assigning its RR (0.85 per 1-MET) to a cardiovascular-mortality-specific marker would misrepresent non-fatal events as deaths, so only the paper's all-cause mortality figure was kept.

cut.label: obesity_bmi -> cardiovascular_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: The Global BMI Mortality Collaboration's headline dose-response figures are for all-cause mortality; no BMI-specific, cleanly quotable cardiovascular-mortality dose-response estimate independent of the all-cause figures already used was retrieved within the research budget.

cut.label: central adiposity / waist circumference as a separate behavior from BMI
cut.reason: A strong dose-response meta-analysis exists (Jayedi 2020, BMJ, waist circumference HR 1.11 per 10cm), but it was not on the candidate behavior list and measures a distinct exposure (central fat distribution) from the requested 'obesity/BMI' behavior; adding it as its own node risked fragmenting the same underlying adiposity concept across two behavior nodes rather than clarifying it.

cut.label: air_pollution_pm25 -> cancer_incidence_mortality, direct PM2.5 (not NO2 proxy) dose-response for lung cancer specifically
cut.reason: A dedicated, cleanly quotable pooled PM2.5-to-lung-cancer dose-response meta-analysis (as distinct from the NO2/traffic-proxy meta-analysis actually used, or the gastrointestinal-cancer PM2.5 meta-analysis found) could not be retrieved within the research budget; the NO2/traffic-proxy edge was shipped instead with an explicit caveat rather than omitting the cancer marker for this behavior entirely.

cut.label: physical activity volume -> cancer_incidence_mortality, quantified
cut.reason: Arem 2015 (JAMA Intern Med, pooled leisure-time physical activity) states in its abstract that 'a similar dose-response relationship was observed for mortality due to cardiovascular disease and to cancer' but does not give a quotable, cancer-specific numeric hazard ratio in the abstract text itself; using it would have required paraphrasing a number not actually present in the verbatim, which the acceptance bar for this file does not allow.

Redundant with the weight_loss_bariatric edges, which already capture the dose-response relationship between adiposity change and liver fat/fibrosis in both directions; no clean, quotable dose-response meta-analysis linking BMI directly to a specific liver marker (independent of a weight-loss intervention) was found within the research budget for this pass.

Search budget was spent on time-restricted eating (TRE) specifically, which had the strongest and most directly comparable RCT evidence (TREATY-FLD); alternate-day and 5:2 fasting protocols for liver markers were not separately verified and are not included to avoid conflating distinct intervention types under one behavior node.

No meta-analysis or adequately powered RCT directly linking sedentary time (as distinct from lack of exercise) to BMD or fracture incidence was located within the research budget for this pass; most literature conflates sedentary time with physical inactivity generally, which would duplicate the resistance_training/impact_exercise/land_based_exercise edges rather than add an independent behavior. Left out rather than asserted from memory; a future pass could search cohort studies using accelerometer-measured sedentary time and site-specific BMD or hip fracture as the outcome.

cut.label: microbiome diversity (alpha-diversity index) as a dedicated marker
cut.reason: Excluded per explicit instruction: alpha-diversity indices have no agreed good direction and no clinical meaning on their own. Several edges above (low-FODMAP diet, Mediterranean-diet-adjacent literature) mention microbiome shifts as a secondary/mechanistic finding in key_results, but no edge uses a diversity index as its primary marker.

cut.label: water intake (plain drinking water) -> stool_frequency_consistency, as a dedicated RCT-supported edge
cut.reason: Only located a cross-sectional, non-interventional study (Mazlyn et al. 2013, Malays J Nutr) among already-constipated Malaysian adults showing a correlation between fluid intake and stool frequency/output (rs=0.257, P<0.05, OR=3.571) - not causal RCT evidence and confounded by the fact that people with worse constipation may also eat and drink less overall. No RCT isolating plain water intake (as opposed to mineral-rich or deep-sea water, which are their own interventions) was located within the research budget. The 2025 British Dietetic Association guideline's water-related recommendations were specifically about high-mineral-content water, not plain water volume, which is consistent with plain water intake alone being a weaker/null intervention - but a clean quantified RCT for that specific null was not retrieved in time.

cut.label: inulin / prebiotic fibre -> any of the four gut markers, as its own dedicated edge
cut.reason: Inulin and other prebiotic fibres were flagged by the task as behaving differently from psyllium and wheat bran and warranting their own row, but a clean, adequately powered inulin-specific RCT or meta-analysis with a quantifiable constipation or IBS outcome (as opposed to fermentation/gas-production or microbiome-composition studies) was not located and fetched within the research budget. Worth a dedicated follow-up search.

cut.label: probiotics by specific single strain (e.g. a single Bifidobacterium or Lactobacillus species) for chronic (non-IBS) constipation specifically
cut.reason: The probiotics edge shipped here uses a class-level IBS meta-analysis (Yang et al. 2024) that pools many strains together, which is a known limitation for a field that explicitly cares about strain-specific effects. A dedicated single-strain, single-indication (chronic constipation rather than IBS) probiotic edge was not extracted within the research budget; the 2025 BDA dietary guideline documents 20 separate probiotic-related recommendation statements, suggesting strain-level extraction is feasible in a follow-up pass.

cut.label: coffee -> ibs_severity or stool_frequency_consistency, as a quantified clinical (not acute-manometric) endpoint
cut.reason: The coffee edge shipped here (Rao et al. 1998) is an acute, small-n (n=12), manometric/mechanistic study, not a clinical trial with a patient-relevant stool-frequency or symptom outcome. A dedicated epidemiological or RCT-based coffee-and-bowel-habit study with a clinical endpoint was not located and fetched within the research budget.

cut.label: Mediterranean diet in PCOS
cut.reason: No dedicated meta-analysis was located that pools a marker-level effect size (testosterone, Ferriman-Gallwey, or menstrual regularity) specifically for a Mediterranean dietary pattern in PCOS. Available trials (e.g. a 12-week RCT combining a Mediterranean/low-carbohydrate pattern vs a low-fat diet in overweight PCOS patients) are single small studies not yet pooled to the evidence bar this file requires. Low-glycaemic-index diet was kept instead because a dedicated systematic review/meta-analysis with quantified outcomes exists (10.1016/j.heliyon.2021.e08338).

cut.label: Alcohol on menstrual symptoms (dysmenorrhoea/PMS)
cut.reason: Evidence found was inconsistent and largely descriptive/cross-sectional (e.g. one Chinese university-student survey found lower rates of dysmenorrhoea among alcohol consumers than non-consumers; others report no association; none met the meta-analysis or adequately powered RCT/cohort bar with a poolable, quantified effect size on a named marker). Smoking was kept because a large pooled cohort analysis with quantified relative risks was available; alcohol was cut for lack of an equivalent quantitative source.

cut.label: Myo-inositol on menstrual cyclicity/ovulation in PCOS
cut.reason: The 2023 PCOS-guideline systematic review and meta-analysis (10.1210/clinem/dgad762, 30 trials, 2230 participants) reports that menstrual-cycle and ovulation outcomes for myo-inositol/D-chiro-inositol were mixed across included studies without a single pooled, quantified effect size meeting this file's verbatim-with-numbers bar. The androgen-outcome edge for myo-inositol (non-significant testosterone SMD) was kept instead, since that number was directly quotable from a dedicated meta-analysis abstract.

cut.label: D-aspartic acid / Tribulus terrestris style 'expected null' supplements for female-specific markers
cut.reason: These were candidates in the male-vitality goal (Goal A) design table, not in this female-health candidate list, and no equivalent PCOS/menopause/PMS-specific supplement trial data for them was sought or found in this pass; not evaluated, not cut on evidence, simply out of scope for this file.

cut.label: Diabetes control (glycemic control level / HbA1c dose-response) -> periodontal_attachment
cut.reason: No meta-analysis quantifying a dose-response between HbA1c/glycemic control level and periodontal attachment loss or probing depth, with a resolvable DOI and quotable verbatim, was found within the research budget. The candidate was narrowed and shipped instead as 'diabetes_status' (diagnosed diabetes vs no diabetes) using a 2026 Lancet Public Health longitudinal meta-analysis (DOI 10.1016/S2468-2667(26)00149-0). An older, frequently cited cross-sectional meta-analysis (Chavarry et al. 2009, Oral Health Prev Dent, clinical attachment level MD 1.00 mm) was found and would have supported a stronger quantitative edge, but has no resolvable DOI in PubMed/Crossref and was excluded on that basis.

cut.label: Xylitol chewing gum -> caries_increment
cut.reason: Corrected rather than cut: the only Cochrane-quality quantitative finding for xylitol products concerns 10% xylitol fluoride TOOTHPASTE (prevented fraction -0.13), not chewing gum specifically; the review does not report a pooled effect for gum as its own category. Shipped as 'xylitol_products' with direction null and the toothpaste-vs-gum distinction made explicit in the caveats, rather than asserting a gum-specific benefit from memory.

cut.label: Professional scaling -> periodontal_attachment (clinical attachment level)
cut.reason: The only Cochrane RCT evidence on routine scale-and-polish (Lamont 2018) explicitly states neither included study measured clinical attachment level. Kept the professional_scaling behavior with a gingival_inflammation null-result edge instead of fabricating an attachment-level number.

cut.label: NMN and blood NAD+ / anti-aging claims sourced from mouse or in vitro studies (e.g. the mechanistic rationale cited in Akasaka 2023 and Fukamizu 2022 abstracts that NMN 'counteracts age-associated changes in animal models')
cut.reason: Explicitly animal-only evidence; importing it as though it applied to humans would misrepresent the current human evidence base, which this file keeps separate.

cut.label: NMN and subjective fatigue/drowsiness (Kim et al. 2022, Nutrients, PMID 35215405, 'Jikaku-sho shirabe' fatigue questionnaire and drowsiness subscale)
cut.reason: No marker in the existing 60-item catalogue or a natural home in any of the 14 existing goals covers subjective fatigue as distinct from sleep quality (PSQI) or mood; the trial's only significant findings were a 5-times-sit-to-stand improvement and a drowsiness reduction specific to afternoon dosing (d=0.64), a narrow, unreplicated, time-of-day-specific result. Forcing it onto m_psqi or perceived_stress would misrepresent what was actually measured. Cut rather than stretched.

cut.label: NMN safety-only trials with no efficacy marker (Fukamizu et al. 2022, Sci Rep, PMID 36002548; 1250 mg/day for 4 weeks, n=31)
cut.reason: This trial reports only that no adverse safety signal exceeded physiological variation; it contains no marker-level efficacy result to attach to any goal. Referenced qualitatively in this file's context but not shipped as an edge.

cut.label: CoQ10 and migraine frequency/duration (Sazali et al. 2021, BMJ Open, PMID 33402403: significant reduction in frequency [MD -1.52/month] and duration [MD -0.19 days], no significant reduction in severity; n=371, 6 RCTs)
cut.reason: This is a real, tier-A, positive finding, but migraine/headache has no corresponding marker or goal in the existing 14-goal graph (the closest goals - mood/anxiety, cognition - do not cover headache disorders, and forcing migraine onto either would misrepresent both the marker and the goal's stated definition). Per the task's instruction to attach only to existing goals, this edge is cut rather than mis-homed. A contradicting 2019 meta-analysis (Can J Neurol Sci, PMID 30764890) found CoQ10 did NOT significantly reduce migraine frequency or severity, so the evidence is not even fully consistent.

cut.label: CoQ10 for diminished ovarian reserve / IVF outcomes in women (PMID 39129455)
cut.reason: This is female reproductive physiology; the existing 'Female reproductive and hormonal health' goal's marker set (vasomotor symptoms, menstrual pain, PMS, PCOS androgens, menstrual regularity) does not include IVF/ovarian-reserve outcomes, and stretching one of those markers to cover oocyte counts and embryo quality would misrepresent both. Noted here rather than forced into an edge.

cut.label: CoQ10 heart-failure NYHA functional class improvement as its own edge (Q-SYMBIO, P=0.028 at 2 years)
cut.reason: No numeric magnitude of NYHA class change is given in the abstract (only a p-value), so no effect size could be derived beyond what is already reported qualitatively in the key_results of the all_cause_mortality edge; a separate edge would duplicate the same trial without adding a quantifiable claim.

cut.label: eleutherococcus_senticosus -> chronic fatigue (Hartz et al. 2004, Randomized controlled trial of Siberian ginseng for chronic fatigue, Psychol Med, PMID 14971626, n=96)
cut.reason: No existing goal or marker in the catalogue covers subjective/chronic fatigue as a named-instrument endpoint (Mood and anxiety is scoped explicitly to PHQ-9/BDI/HAM-D, GAD-7/STAI/HAM-A/BAI, PSS, and cortisol; Cognition and focus, Immune function, and the other 12 goals do not cover it either). The trial itself also found overall efficacy 'not demonstrated', with only a subgroup hint of benefit in less-severe or long-duration fatigue. Rather than inventing a new goal or forcing this onto a mismatched marker, it is left uncaptured; a future 'fatigue/energy' goal would be the right home for it.

cut.label: american_ginseng -> cancer-related fatigue (Barton et al. 2013, Wisconsin Ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) to Improve Cancer-Related Fatigue: N07C2, J Natl Cancer Inst, PMID 23853057, n=364)
cut.reason: This is the single strongest RCT found for any ginseng species in this research pass (n=364, phase III, significant dose-response-consistent benefit: MFSI-SF change score 20 vs 10.3, P=.003 at 8 weeks), but like the Eleutherococcus fatigue trial above it has no home in the current 14-goal, 60-marker catalogue, which does not include a fatigue/vitality-energy goal. Cut here rather than mis-attached to Mood and anxiety or Male vitality, neither of which defines fatigue as an in-scope marker.

cut.label: CVT-E002 (North American ginseng) for URI prevention in institutionalized older adults (McElhaney et al. 2004, PMID 14687309)
cut.reason: A companion, earlier trial of the same COLD-fX extract in a frailer institutionalized-senior population was identified by search but its abstract was not retrieved and verified within the research budget for this file; the community-dwelling, influenza-vaccinated version of this trial (McElhaney 2011) is shipped instead.

cut.label: Cochrane review 'Ginseng for cognition' (Geng et al. 2010) as an additional cognition source
cut.reason: This earlier Cochrane review (9 RCTs) reports that pooling was 'impossible due to heterogeneity in outcome measures, trial duration, and ginseng dosage' per secondary summaries found during search, i.e. it does not offer a quantified, verbatim-derivable effect size of its own. Superseded here by the two more recent, quantified 2024/2025 meta-analyses (Zeng et al.; Kim et al.) that are shipped as ginseng_species_unspecified edges above.

cut.label: Panax ginseng for menopausal vasomotor symptoms or PCOS androgen markers (Female reproductive and hormonal health goal)
cut.reason: Not investigated within this research pass's time budget; the brief's listed likely endpoints (cognition, fatigue, erectile function, glucose/HbA1c, blood pressure, URI incidence, immune measures) were prioritized first. Flagged as a plausible follow-up search rather than asserted from memory.

cut.label: Rg3-enriched Korean Red Ginseng + American ginseng coadministration trial for cardiometabolic outcomes in type-2 diabetes (PMID 34803424)
cut.reason: This trial deliberately combines Korean Red Ginseng (Panax ginseng) and American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) as a co-administered product, which is a genuine third condition (neither single-species nor an unstratified pooled review, but a combination product tested as such). Not shipped here because its abstract was not retrieved and verified within the research budget; flagged rather than asserted, and would need its own conditional_on describing the co-administration explicitly rather than being folded into either single-species behavior or the pooled-review behavior above.

cut.label: Metformin in PCOS
cut.reason: A prescription drug for PCOS, not something a reader chooses. It arrived grouped with supplements, which put a prescribed medicine beside vitamin D and fish oil.

cut.label: NSAIDs for dysmenorrhoea
cut.reason: A prescription-strength analgesic regimen, not a behaviour a reader adopts. Same misgrouping.

cut.label: Intensive blood pressure control (systolic <120 mmHg)
cut.reason: Intensive antihypertensive treatment to a systolic target of 120 mmHg. Nobody reaches this without first being diagnosed and treated for hypertension, so it is not a decision a reader arrives at - it is one their doctor makes for them once they are already in the system. Same reasoning as metformin for PCOS.

cut.label: Diabetes (type 1/2/gestational) status
cut.reason: Having diabetes or not is a health condition, not something a reader chooses to do. The finding it carried - that diabetes raises the risk of incident periodontitis - is real, but a page about what to do is the wrong shape for it: there is no behaviour on the other end of the arrow. It had also fallen into the mind-and-social group, which made no sense either.
